subject: Social Media
title: Engagement Bait
description: A micro-lesson that makes Engagement Bait usable.

hook.text: 'Tag a friend who does this!' 'Like if you agree!' These posts hack the algorithm with forced actions.

buildup.text: Facebook labeled these 'engagement bait' in 2017 and penalized pages using the tactic.

discovery.text: It worked because algorithms count actions, not intent. A forced like and a real like look identical.

twist.text: Creators pivoted to subtle bait—questions, polls, and hot takes designed to provoke comments.

climax.text: The arms race never ends. Platforms update rules; creators find loopholes. The game resets itself.

punchline.text: Ban the trick and a new one grows.

quiz.question: Why did engagement bait work on algorithms?
options: Algorithms counted actions regardless of intent
